sections.html:
Polk County had 42,853 residents at the 2020 census and an estimated 45,514 in July 2025. Cedartown and Rockmart each host a tax commissioner office.

Homes here are among the lower priced in the area. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $187,600, rent is about $918 a month, and the median household income is $58,515. Owners live in 66.0% of housing, so about one home in three is a rental. A landlord selling a rental should expect questions about leases and tenant access. The county has 17,654 housing units and 15,901 households, and 217 building permits were issued in 2025, so new construction is thin next to the existing stock. Housing costs run $1,428 a month with a mortgage and $502 without. The average commute is 30.5 minutes.

The buyer pool is mostly local and budget-conscious, and many buyers rely on a mortgage and a clean title. A house that arrives at the table with its tax paid and no recorded FIFA gives a financed buyer fewer reasons to hesitate.

sections.h2: Where are the Polk County tax offices?
sections.html:
There are two counters, both open weekdays from 9 am to 5 pm and shut for lunch from 12:45 to 2:00.

  • Cedartown: 144 West Ave, GA 30125.
  • Rockmart: 316 N Piedmont Ave, GA 30153.
  • Shared contact: (770) 749-2125 or taxoffice@polkga.org.
  • Assessors: (770) 749-2108.

City tax is not billed by the county. Each city sends its own, so a Rockmart or Cedartown seller may need a payoff from the city clerk in addition to the county. The county does not sell tax liens.

The usual due date is December 20, though the county commissioner's page also describes payment as due sixty days after the bill is mailed. Check the date printed on your bill, since that one controls.

Interest of 1% a month starts after the due date, and a 10% penalty hits anything still open at 90 days. A homestead parcel owing under $500 skips that penalty. Once 90 days pass, the tax office may record a FIFA at the Clerk of Superior Court. The record is public, and it can show up in credit reports.

A bill is mailed to the owner and not to a lender. If a mortgage company escrows your tax, forward the bill to the servicer and include your loan number.

The Board of Assessors mails notices each summer. Each notice starts a 45-day appeal clock, so respond inside that window or the value stands for the year.

The county directs owners to qpublic.net/ga/polk to see property characteristics, ownership, assessed values, parcel maps and sales history. Its tax estimator asks you to choose the right tax district, choose Not Exempt, key in the market value on the notice, and then subtract the estimated tax savings printed on the notice. The result is an estimate only, because final millage rates may differ.

An appeal goes to the assessors first. A dispute that stays open can move on to the Grand Jury's appointed Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator, with a superior court filing available after that.

To qualify you must have held title on January 1, treat the house as your legal residence, live there, and claim no homestead elsewhere. You can file any time of year, but the form must arrive before April 1 to change that year's bill.

Polk County homestead exemptions
ExemptionWhat it takes off
Standard homesteadFirst $2,000 of assessed value, on county, state and school tax
Age 65$20,000 off school tax and $4,000 off county tax
Age 62, owner and spouse income under $10,000Extra relief
Age 70, household income under $10,000Extra relief
Veteran who is 100% permanently disabledAn added exemption

Only your primary home can be homesteaded, and a move means a fresh application.

sections.h2: Selling a rental in Polk County
sections.html:
With about one home in three occupied by someone other than the owner, plenty of sales here involve a tenant. The tax side of that sale is the same as for any other house: the bill follows the parcel, and the payoff comes out of your proceeds.

The practical issues come from the lease. A buyer who wants to live in the house needs the tenant out first, and a buyer who wants a rental needs the lease terms and the deposit record. Showings need notice and access. If any of that is slowing a standard listing, a cash buyer can take the house with the tenant in place or on a closing date that fits the lease, and the tax still gets settled on the statement.

Landlords sometimes hold more than a house. Owners who also run a business may have equipment on the tax rolls, which means another bill and another payoff to request before closing.

A regular listing leans on the buyer's loan, the appraisal and haggling over repairs. Each step can stall a sale when the house has a tax balance, a recorded FIFA or deferred work. A cash sale removes the loan and the appraisal, so the timeline depends mostly on how fast the title company can get the payoffs from the county and, if needed, the city.

The order is simple. You request the balances, the title company confirms them in writing, the buyer's offer is compared with a standard listing after repairs and holding costs, and the payoffs are listed on the settlement statement. The county gets paid from the sale money, and the rest is yours. Weigh any offer against what a listing would put in your pocket.

sections.h2: How do I close a Polk County sale when tax is owed?
sections.html:
Get the numbers first and pay them from the sale proceeds. The commissioner does not sell tax liens, but a recorded FIFA still clouds the title until it is satisfied.

  1. Phone (770) 749-2125 for the balance, with interest and penalty.
  2. Ask if a FIFA is on file.
  3. Request a city payoff when the house sits inside city limits.
  4. Put each amount on the settlement statement.

If a tenant, a repair list or an inherited deed is slowing a standard listing, an as-is cash buyer can work around them and settle the tax at closing.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
Call either counter first and say you are selling. Ask what you owe, interest and penalty included. Two offices can matter, so ask the same question of the city clerk if your house sits inside Cedartown or Rockmart.

  • The bill itself, which shows the due date that applies to your parcel.
  • Proof of homestead, if you claim it, so the buyer's lender sees the right tax figure.
  • Lease copies and tenant contact details, if you are selling a rental.
  • Your loan number, if a servicer pays the tax from escrow.

Ask the closing attorney to list each payoff on the settlement statement. Keep a signed copy, since it is your proof of who paid what if a question comes up later.

faqs.q: What is the Polk County due date for tax?
faqs.a: The bill itself controls. The usual date is December 20, and the commissioner's page also describes payment sixty days after the mailing date.

faqs.q: How much interest does Polk County charge?
faqs.a: Interest is 1% a month starting after the due date, with a 10% penalty at the 90-day mark.

faqs.q: Where do Polk County residents pay tax in person?
faqs.a: At 144 West Ave in Cedartown or 316 N Piedmont Ave in Rockmart, on weekdays from 9 am to 5 pm.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Polk County value?
faqs.a: Each assessment notice starts a 45-day clock. File with the assessors first, then the Board of Equalization or arbitration if needed.

faqs.q: Does Polk County bill city tax too?
faqs.a: No. Cities within Polk send their own bills, so request that balance from the city clerk before the closing date.
